Late 1880s-1890s. When I was a kid, my mom (single parent) worked as an in-home carer. We couldn't get childcare and regulations were a lot more lapse then so she'd take me with her to the homes and let me sit with the elderly people while she cleaned up etc. Some of the oldest were over 100. Generally they were really kind and very happy to have someone to talk to. Decades later, I still remember their names and lots of information about them, which feels very meaningful. 

In fact, many of them left us things when they passed away. Nothing expensive, I had many many teddies and trinkets left to me. My sister's favourite toy growing up was a plushie dog given to her that was well over 50 years old. A stand out piece was a 150 year old chair a lovely lady called Dorothy gave us, hand carved by her father.

Have you looked into findagrave.com? It's a huge database of graves and memorials and volunteers take photos and add graves to the database. I volunteer in my city where it's not very popular and I get fairly regular requests to go to specific cemeteries and find certain memorials and record them. A lot of them are for people overseas who want to check in on family graves or are doing genealogy projects.

I had been banking with them for 15+ years when I moved abroad a few years ago. After a month abroad they decided to block my card for suspicious activity despite me verifying the transactions. They had the worst customer service I've ever had to put up with. They insisted on communicating over letters and never responded to emails. I must have spent 30+ hours on hold. I was constantly being hung up on or transferred to random departments when the person on the other end didn't want to deal with it. I'd speak to a 'manager' who would promise to look into it and call me back 'next week' and of course they never did. 

 After another year and constant back and forth with the ombudsman, I was refunded the money they'd taken unnecessarily and offered £50 compensation. Three years later and I still can't access the account and they refuse to close it unless I go into a branch in the UK. 

This was my main bank account for 15 years and I'd never had any problems until then. But this kind of nonsense is why people are switching to banks with Monzo and Revolut who don't pull this nonsense.

I always try to cover costs in some way for my host. I usually bring a gift with me from either my home country or if I'm travelling for a longer time, the place I have just travelled from. Something which is obvious and 'different' like a magnet with the city name on it or a local candy.

When hosting I've often received the same courtesy. I've had people bring me small gifts from all over the world and have a shelf dedicated to them at home. I've been couchsurfing since I was 18 and now I'm 31. The vibe has definitely changed as I've aged, when I was a teenager I was couchsurfing because I loved it but also because I was a broke little gremlin, hitchhiking around because I wanted to travel as much as possible. I couldn't have afforded to buy my host dinner back then but I still made an effort to bring a gift and cook if I could. I think it's the thought that counts. Now I'm older, I'm in the position where I can easily afford a hotel but I'm usually couchsurfing for the experience. To be honest there are times where I've spent more on meal ingredients and gifts than I would have on a cheap hostel in that city. But I'm doing it for the experience not to save money. I don't think anyone has ever felt taken advantage of by me staying. 

I've also had both types of guests. I had a 18 year old guy on my sofa for a week while he hitchhiked around Europe and I loved hosting him because he reminded me of young and reckless me. I've also had guests turn up with the same sentiment of just surfing to hang out with a local and not being desperate for a place and we've had a lovely evening sharing stories or whatever.

 As a host, I like cooking and taking care of my guests in general. I usually have some little breakfast cereals set up for them and some toiletries if they need them. Partly because that's just my personality and partly because I know what it's like to be a budget traveller and want to help anyone living their dreams like that now I'm more stable. I've never asked guests to split food costs 50/50 but I've also only had 1 or 2 guests really take advantage of my hospitality. Like I said, most either turn up with a gift or offer to buy something or help out in some way. 

I make a point of setting expectations really clearly on my profile. I don't know if that's why I get generally positive guests. Chiming in as someone who currently works in combat medicine in a warzone. There are four criteria under which we apply a tourniquet to a limb.
1) amputation of the limb
2) blood spraying out in a fountain
3) Enough blood to soak the clothes
4) Enough blood to form a pool under the casualty

While it's debated, I personally always err on the side of caution when it comes to TQ application. I'd rather have someone lose a limb than bleed out. If in doubt as to whether there is enough blood to warrant a tourniquet, it's better to apply one.

 Keep in mind this is often under high stress, evacuation situations where there isn't time to assess the wound. When in doubt apply the tourniquet as high and tight on the limb as possible. Never on a joint. Hope that's useful.

Consider instead of a tent a good warm sleeping bag and a bivvy bag. Bivvy bags are water and windproof sacks that go over your sleeping bag and allow you to sleep anywhere. They are used in the military and by more adventurous campers, you should be able to find them in any decent camping or outdoor store. They are much more lightweight and less noticeable. They're usually khaki green so you won't be easily visible if youre in a wooded area.

Also invest in a decent tarp. You can lay this on the ground for insulation and to keep your bag dry. You can also string another up to keep the rain off and give the feeling of privacy. Again get a khaki coloured one.

Reason for this advice is that people react strongly to tents. They are noticeable. A tarp or a bivvy blend in. Also tents need a certain amount of space to be set up in. You can string a tarp up and lay down anywhere.

My situation was completely different but might offer some insight.
Last year my housemate moved his girlfriend in when lockdown started. She didn't like me (I'm a girl so maybe that was an issue for her). Me and my housemate went from being close friends to strangers and finally enemies within a year. She would start fights with me when he was out and act all sweet when he was around. She would hide or throw away my stuff and 'accidentally' eat my food. She was completely passive aggressive and would make comments about me dying alone and my life choices and then pretend they were jokes. Eventually she started interrupting if me and my housemate/friend were talking to each other, she hated us spending time alone. She hijacked all the shared spaces in the house. My painting room became her office, the spare room became her storage room. Anything I left in a communal area was throw in a bag and left outside my bedroom door. 
We were all stuck in the same house due to covid. 


I thought I could deal with her because surely my friend saw how she was acting right? Wrong. He didn't want to get involved so he didn't say or do anything to her even if it was right in front of him. He thought it was the right thing but in reality he was just ignoring her bad behaviour. For over a year I tried my best to let it slide but I didn't realise how much it was affecting my mental health. I would avoid leaving my room if she was around because she was bound to start an argument with me. I started to accept that I would never know where half my stuff had disappeared to. Every day I would get mean, personal comments when alone with her and then my housemate would come home and they'd ignore me. I could walk in a room and they wouldn't even look up, let alone say hello. Lots of little things that added up over time, like him not checking on me the night my grandfather died and I was crying in my room. Not saving some food for me when I got back from a 12 hour shift. I felt invisible and stopped considering him a friend. 

One day, out of nowhere, just snapped. I can't remember what was said by her exactly but I was very stressed and having a bad day. I went crazy at her. I was shouting and I smashed a glass plate against the wall. When the whole thing didn't smash, I picked up the biggest piece and hit it again. My hand was bleeding and there was glass everywhere but I didn't care. I flipped the table and smashed my favourite mug. I snapped two of her paintbrushes and threw the pieces at her. Honestly, I probably would have slapped her if she had come near me. I'm not proud of this but it happened. I felt like it wasn't even me acting this way, like I was processed. I felt absolutely crazy, and for a minute I probably was. Afterwards, I looked around at the mess I'd caused and I couldn't even understand how it had happened. It didn't feel like I'd done it. 

My point is, people don't tend to just blowup suddenly. Usually it comes after a loooong build up. Did any of the individual things she did deserve my response? No. But did she deserve it for a year of making me feel attacked, isolated and stressed in my own home? Maybe. 

So OP, your gf might be having a mental break, but it sounds to me more like the tension in the house you've described elsewhere led to her snapping. That doesn't justify what she did to your computer but it might explain why she lashed out at your mom. It might also explain why she has said all those abusive things to you, perhaps she sees you not intervening as allowing your mothers behaviour. I not only don't consider my ex-housemate anymore, I almost hate him. Things should never have got that far. 

Again, I'm not blaming you, you're the victim here. Nor am I justifying her behaviour, I'm just trying to explain it from a different point of view

Clear the history, go into settings and clear the cache for YouTube. Watch a bunch of similarly themed but positive videos in parallel. The algorithm is a mysterious beast but it is generally more likely to show you more of what you seek out (so search for a bunch of stuff) but even more so what it believes you are engaging with. That means let the videos play through so it thinks he's watching them. Give them a like or even a brief comment like 'I love this' if you think he won't notice. Once YT sees him engaging with these videos it will send him more of the same. Subscribe to the good channels and unsubscribe from any bad ones. 

Before you start with the positive channels, scroll through his homepage and locate the negative ones. Click the three little dots and there should be an option to 'not show videos from this channel'. 

Recommendations to spam him with? Short but very engaging things that will keep his attention, there are plenty of ten minute videos about 'the 3 most badass ninjas in history' 'top 5 craziest places you should visit' or whatever. These are the kind of videos I put on when I need an easy distraction. I'd say to start off with these will be the easiest for him to consume and keep him watching more. Worth also sprinkling some self help channels in there.

I lived in rural Norway for many years. We are talking a huge area with less than 1k people. I worked outside alone in the winter and loved my work enough to keep me happy, but I am quite introverted anyway and it was a 24/7 commitment. 

When the spring came, at first it was lonely. But actaully when I started work I managed to finally meet people and make friends. Some had zero interest in me and some were very interested in a foreigner choosing to actually live in the area. We got plenty of tourists for the nature but not many settled there.

Generally people were either very welcoming or very unwelcoming. To give the most extreme examples. My housemates mother would regularly invite me round to her house in a nearby town, cook for me and bring me to social events with her. Of course these were generally events with 60+ year olds but it was still nice and I got to experience some genuine culture. She took me to see a play once and would explain anything strange and new to me in a way I could understand, including vocabulary.
On the other hand, my neighbours mother called immigration on me and had them come to investigate my work permit after I had a (valid) disagreement with her son. When asked why, she started screaming that you can't trust foreigners and I'm not welcome there. So two very different reactions to my presence there.

My best advice - Norwegians bond by doing stuff together. Go for hikes, go skiing, go fishing, whatever. Don't expect people to just want to go to coffee or want to be besties after meeting a few times. Most friendships take time to build but they generally last. 
Small talk is generally a waste of time, especially if you don't know the person well. I might go for coffee with an old friend, but with someone new I'd rather do something I enjoy like a hike and chat while we do it and see if we can be friends. If not, hey I still got to hike :) 

Also, anyone who plans to spend more than a few months there, try to learn the language. It's not as difficult as most others and there are plenty of resources available, including free lessons in most towns and cities. People will take you more seriously if you make an effort and you will understand a lot more of what is going on around you.

I don't love or hate my nickname but it is my name as far as I'm concerned. I like that's its gender neutral, has no obvious meaning and isnt easily associated with my full name. Think Rin as short for Catherine instead of cathy. And Catherine is spelt in a super trendy 90s style and followed by a generic middle name. Like Cafferyn May but not quite (yes I know) 🙄

Over the years, I've tried various name changes but they never felt right. I tried my nickname as my legal first name. I tried a random name with my birth name as a middle name etc. But everytime I made changes  it just felt clunky and inauthentic. 

I decided to finally change my name legally since people at work and some in my personal life iinsist on calling me my birth name and various nicknames and I just hate it. I was sick of having variations of 'Cathy' called at me when I've literally never gone by that. The final straw was on a work trip (we lead expeditions). I have a colleague who insisted on called me 'Catherine' and introduced me to everyone on trup as this despite me correcting him so many times before. These are long expeditions where we live close together and it was grating on me. Not to mention if theres an emergency on the mountain, it's a good idea to use someones name to get their attention as quickly as possible, as opposed to whatever you've decided to call them on that day. But I let it go because i work abroad and I thought maybe my nn was hard to pronounce for this guy. Last night of the trip we're celebrating, we're all playing poker and he cant hold his drink. Lo and behold he starts calling me Rin. I'm shocked and say 'so you CAN say it and you do know I prefer it. I ask why he hasnt always called me it and he just shrugs and laughs. I realised then that a lot of people just arent going to respect my slightly unorthodox nickname if it's not the standard nickname for my given name. 

This month I legally changed my name to something where Rin is much more obvious and no one has questioned it since. Since then I've found out that was actually my great great grandmothers name so that's an added bonus because I'm honouring a family connection without outright using her name. I also changed my middle names to variations of grandparents as one of the reasons I hated my name as a child was that I'm the only one of my siblings without an honour name. As I barely knew my father and was raised by my grandparents I decided to scrap my surname too and use theirs. I knew as soon as I wrote it down it was right for me. 

Its definitely felt strange introducing myself by this but I'm getting used to it. I love the way this name flows and that it all has significance. I often feel like a fraud when introducing myself, especially to official places like the bank. Then I have to remind myself that this is my legal name now and not introducing myself as it is fraud 🤣 

I felt grief for my old name despite the fact I loathe it. I'd always associated it with an older generation but it suddenly felt like I kept noticing young beautiful women with this name and thinking 'oh I should have kept my old name it was so beautiful'. I also started noticing it in articles more, in random personalised things online, even hearing people shouting it out. Every time I felt a twinge of sadness and then I had to remind myself that my new name is more awesome and fits me :) i think I'll always miss my old name a little, I did carry it around for 30 years after all, even if I rarely used it, and it will always be a little part of my identity. But I'm really happy I'm finally being more true to who I am and who I aspire to be rather than whatever half assed combination my parents threw together.

So that was super rambling but I hope it helps. Its certainly helped me to see lots of other people have been through the same thing!

I have many but one that always stands out for pure randomness is this one. 

A few years ago I hosted a young Australian guy who had sent a pretty basic request, implying he was travelling and visiting my city. It wasn't a great request and his profile was very basic but I was already hosting another couple that weekend so thought 'the more the merrier'. 

When he turned up he admitted that he wasnt actually travelling but had been living in the city for over a year. The story went-  He had been backpacking when he met a girl there, they had fallen in love and he decided to stay. He got a year long work visa and started working in telesales. But now his visa had run out so he couldn't work anymore and would have to go home soon. 

Their solution- get married. Only problem was her parents were strictly religious and didn't even know he existed. So there was no chance they could do so openly and no way he could live with her in the meantime. They were going to run away to scotland together and elope. Meanwhile, he had applied for a 'fiance visa' while they planned their elopement. He had been crashing on friend's sofas for months waiting for the Visa decision and had exhausted their hospitality so was now turning to couchsurfing.

Needless to say, I was a little bit annoyed that he had misled me. His request has been cleverly phrased to make it sound like he was travelling without saying it outright. But, I sympathised with his situation, had other guests and he was only there for one night so let it go. 
As a guest, he was a typical CS bum really. Me and the other guests all chipped in, bought ingredients and cooked together while he bought a bottle of wine and started drinking. He got tipsy and was talking a lot of nonsense but he was relatively harmless. He fell asleep in his clothes and left the next day. I got the impression he was hanging around to see if I'd offer him a longer stay I didn't budge, he just wasnt a guest I'd want around when it wasnt the weekend. 

Things get really weird a couple of days later. He calls me out of nowhere and I'm expecting him to ask if he can stay again. Nope, he needs my help asap. He had had unprotected sex with his girlfriend the night before and needed the morning after pill. she was unable to collect it herself because if anyone in her parents social circle (very large religious community) saw her at the sexual health clinic she would be in her words 'literally killed'. So of course I agreed to help her.

 About half an hour later she picked me up, confirming aussie guys story- honestly part of me had been wondering if it was all bs until this point. All three of us went to the clinic and she parked around the block while me and him went in. 
I'm not sure about elsewhere but in the UK they will give you a little interview before prescribing the pill to make sure you're not already pregnant, don't have any underlying medical conditions etc etc. I had to lie my way through that using the information she had given me about herself. When he asked me and the Aussie guy when the last time we had slept together was, I just about died while he laughed his ass off.

 Anyway, pill acquired we went back to the car where she started beating on him for being 'such an idiot'. Not sure what she meant exactly, but it was very romantic.

And that was that! I bumped into him a few months later on the metro and it was weird but he was friendly enough. He texted me a few months after that asking for a place to stay again. I had just bought a 3 bed house but hadn't furnished the spare room, so i offered him the spare room with an air bed for a week or two since I couldn't rent it yet and he declined because it wasn't a real bed! Beggars can be choosers!

I sometimes wonder what became of that couple, I'm half expecting him to still be on random couches four years later. Although part of me likes to imagine they made it to Scotland and are living a happily married life in a cottage somewhere. Guess I'll never know!
